root_cause_summary: runCalendarConsolidation loads rows without tenant identity and invokes consolidateCalendar once over the global active-row set, so threshold selection and sourceIds are computed across tenant boundaries before insertion and superseding.
affected_code: services/calendar-consolidation.js: loadActiveCalendarRows lines 12-20 and runCalendarConsolidation lines 71-110
localization_analysis: The executed reproducer reached runCalendarConsolidation and the project-source trace captured fourteen loaded IDs with user_id and companion_id absent, matching the select projection at line 15. The next trace captured a single week job whose sourceIds alternate between user-a and user-b, directly matching the unpartitioned consolidateCalendar(activeRows) call. The failing assertion confirms the runtime impact: one mixed summary was inserted instead of two tenant-local summaries. The subsequent sourceRows filter and markSuperseded consume that mixed sourceIds list, extending the same isolation violation to insertion metadata and source updates. This is a local implementation logic defect in the calendar consolidation orchestration.
